text:
sara-support: FYI customers are hitting 502/504 and heavy tail latencies for streaming/generate in ap-southeast-1. Support queue has 6 escalations. Logs show upstream resets.

mike-netops: I see a big spike in TCP retransmits and out-of-order acks on egress toward ISP-A starting ~13:02 UTC. Flow logs show bursts of ~5-10% packet retransmit on the peering leg.

julia-sre: No infra deploys in that timeframe per deploy-bot. deploy-bot: deploy finished 12:55 UTC to canary only.

kevin-ops: Confirming edge LB metrics: active streaming connections increased RTOs and connection resets; 502s correlate with connections with >60s lifetimes (streaming).

sara-support: Customer-acme posted repro: long-running streaming call fails after ~30s with 502. They attached curl test.

customer-acme: repro steps (sanitized):
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-rls","stream":true,"prompt":"...long prompt..."}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
Result: stream starts then connection resets with HTTP/1.1 502 and no more chunks.

mike-netops: tcpdump from edge (ap-southeast-1-e1):
```
13:02:14.123 IP host.xxx > isp-a.net: Flags [P.], seq 123:456, ack 789, win 65535
13:02:14.223 IP host.xxx > isp-a.net: Retransmission, seq 123:456
13:02:14.324 IP isp-a.net > host.xxx: Dup ACK 789
```
This looks like egress queuing/reorder or a shaping microburst on ISP-A.

julia-sre: Any BGP changes?

mike-netops: No BGP adj changes in control plane. Looks like congestion/queue overflow at ISP egress or aggregation device. We also see increase in HTTP upstream resets from our edge-to-transit sockets.

kevin-ops: I've raised NOC ticket with ISP-A: ticket #NOC-8219, they acknowledged intermittent queueing on an interconnect, said they're rolling a config change.

sara-support: Action items: 1) Fail traffic to backup transit (isp-b) for ap-southeast-1 egress. 2) Notify impacted customers with ETA. 3) Start capturing long-stream tcp logs and correlate customer keys for billing/credits. 4) Prepare rollback if failover causes regressions.

mike-netops: Kicking BGP prepends to prefer ISP-B now for egress from ap-southeast-1 edge nodes. Applying in /ops/bgp/egress-apse1: prepended 2 to ISP-B, withdraw some communities to prefer backup.

deploy-bot: route-change job started at 13:10 UTC.

kevin-ops: Failover completed 13:13 UTC. Post-failover metrics: retransmit rate dropped to baseline, 502s for streaming reduced from 6% -> 0.5% in the last 10m.

customer-acme: We see traffic stabilized, thanks. Can you confirm whether we'll get credits for increased error rate during the incident window? We had production traffic affected.

sara-support: We'll file a billing escalation and include error windows and retry counts. Please DM support case #4621 with any detailed request.

julia-sre: Root-cause notes for postmortem: transient egress queueing at ISP-A causing packet retransmit/reorder and resets for long-lived streaming connections. Contributing factors: high sustained streaming concurrency in ap-southeast-1 + single preferred transit (failover uncovered).

kevin-ops: Temporary mitigations applied: BGP failover to ISP-B, reduce keepalive idle to 30s on edge proxy for streaming sockets, increase upstream socket send buffer to tolerate brief microbursts.

mike-netops: Long-term: engage ISP-A for SLO on interconnect jitter, add second physical cross-connect for diversity, automation to detect retransmit spikes and auto-prepend to backup.

sara-support: Customer comms draft: "We experienced intermittent egress network congestion to ISP-A in ap-southeast-1 causing increased errors on streaming endpoints. We failed traffic to a backup transit and errors have returned to normal. We will follow up with RCA and billing options."

customer-acme: Appreciate the update. Please share the postmortem and narrow window for credits.

julia-sre: Assigning postmortem to @julia-sre, collectors: tcpdumps, flow logs, edge proxy traces, customer request logs. Target PM: 24h prelim RCA, full RCA within 72h.

kevin-ops: Closing incident channel after postmortem. Current status: mitigated, monitoring for recurrence.
